notes: Hook checked: a part-closed discharge valve usually lowers a centrifugal pump motor's current. Research backs it: at no flow the power the motor needs is at or near its minimum, and the motor's current rises as flow rises. The word usually keeps it hedged.

In one breath overclaimed: "though never all of it into work" dropped the source's qualifier, which is a cyclical process. A single stroke can turn all its heat into work, for example a gas expanding at steady temperature. Corrected in topic.json to "though an engine running in a repeating cycle can never turn all of it into work."

The rest of In one breath checked against the research and the i1 lesson: heat flows from hotter to colder; melting and boiling take in energy at a steady temperature; pressure grows with depth and the difference gives upthrust; a narrowing trades pressure for speed; a pump settles where its curve crosses the pipe's.
